symptom: On the after-startup runner (every Docker run, and `--local --legacy-runner`) a test with more than one `@expect` is reported PASS when an earlier assertion fails and a later one passes, and `mxcli test` exits 0. Measured at unit level: log FAIL:test_1:Expected $r = 1, actual: 2 then PASS:test_1 gave status=PASS message="" AllPassed=true. PASS then FAIL reported correctly; the endpoint runner (`--local`, `--attach`, `--watch`) was never affected
cause: `writeExpectAssertion` logs a verdict line per assertion (MXTEST:PASS or MXTEST:FAIL), and `ParseLogResults` treated every line as the test's verdict: each case overwrote Status, and the PASS case also cleared Message, so the last line won. The generated flow did compute `$AllPassed = false` and return it — nothing reads that value
insight: A log protocol that emits several partial verdicts per test needs a monotonic fold, not last-write-wins: FAIL/ERROR is sticky, the first failure's message is reported (the endpoint runner's semantics — its assertions run only while $Verdict is PASS and its skipped-assertions guard never replaces a failure), and further failures are counted onto the message. The plausible wrong turn is 'first verdict line wins': the skipped-assertions guard (#1448) logs its FAIL AFTER the PASS lines of the assertions that did run, so first-wins turns that false green back on — sticky failure, not first line, is the rule. Fixed in the parser rather than the generator: it also corrects logs from runners generated before the fix, and a one-verdict-per-test generator would change a flow shape whose verdicts were measured on 11.13.0 for no additional coverage, since parser and generator ship in one binary. A RUN line resets the fold so a failure cannot outlive the run it was logged in. Second time this parser took a verdict from the wrong line (after #1448's RUN-without-verdict read as the zero status, PASS): when touching `ParseLogResults`, enumerate the line ORDERS the generator can produce per test, not just the line kinds
